## TL;DR

The task drawer's footer action row and its three confirmation dialogs no longer
repeat the word "task". The footer buttons now read exactly **Delete**,
**Archive** and **Hold** (with **Release hold** when held and **Unarchive**
already correct for archived tasks), and the confirm buttons inside
DeleteTaskDialog, ArchiveTaskDialog and HoldTaskDialog read **Delete**,
**Archive** and **Hold** respectively, while the dialog titles keep their
context-bearing wording ("Delete task?", "Archive task?", "Hold task"). The
footer buttons gained descriptive `aria-label` attributes ("Delete task",
"Archive task") so screen-reader users still hear what is affected, per the
task's note. Four test files, two user-docs pages and four code comments that
quoted the old labels were updated to match. The scoped check
(`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`) passes end to end, and the five
directly affected test files pass locally (43 tests).

## Work and rationale

The change is deliberately tiny — it is a copy-editing task, and the whole risk
is in the places that *assert* or *document* the old copy, not in the copy
itself.

**Footer buttons (TaskDrawer.vue, details tab `.delete-zone`).** "Delete task"
→ "Delete" and "Archive task" → "Archive". "Hold" and "Release hold" were
already the desired shapes, so they are untouched. I added `aria-label="Delete
task"` and `aria-label="Archive task"` because a one-word "Delete" button is
ambiguous out of context for assistive tech; the visible label gets shorter,
the accessible name does not. `data-test-id="archive-task"` stays as-is — it
identifies the control, not its caption, and renaming it would churn unrelated
tests for no user-visible gain.

**Confirmation dialogs.** Only the confirm buttons changed ("Delete task" →
"Delete", etc.). The titles intentionally keep "task": on a bare dialog with no
drawer around it, "Delete task?" is the right amount of specificity, which is
exactly the distinction the task drew. The `Deleting…`/`Archiving…`/`Holding…`
busy states were already free of the word "task".

**Tests.** `task-drawer-held.test.ts` asserted the footer row as
`["Delete task", "Archive task", "Hold"]` — now `["Delete", "Archive", "Hold"]`.
Two tests located the Hold dialog's submit button with
`text().includes("Hold task")`; since the button no longer says that, I switched
both to an exact match (`text().trim() === "Hold"`), which also makes them
immune to a future "Holding…" busy-state overlap. In `task-archive-ui.test.ts`
the archived-drawer assertions used `toContain("Delete task")` /
`not.toContain("Archive task")`. I replaced the positive assertion with
`toContain("Delete")` and made the negative one structural — the archive button
must not exist (`[data-test-id="archive-task"]`) — while keeping the string
assertion. Rationale: with shorter labels, loose substring assertions get
brittle in both directions ("Unarchive" does not contain capital-A "Archive",
but a future archive-reason card could easily contain the word), so the test
now pins the element, not the prose.

**Docs.** `user-docs/review-and-close-out.md` and `user-docs/concepts.md` both
instructed users to click "**Archive task**"; they now say "**Archive**". Four
code comments (InputsView.vue, StoryPanel.vue, and the header comments of
`input-story-delete-ui.test.ts`) referenced "the task panel's Delete task" as a
positioning reference; they now say "Delete button". Historical records —
`work/<id>-*.md` task files, CHANGELOG.md, release-history.json,
docs/field-reports, HANDOFF-2026-11-02.md — are immutable history and were left
alone; none of them describes current UI behaviour in a way that misleads.

**Shots.** I declared one shot for review: the drawer's details tab with the
`drawer:reviewWithBranch` fixture, selecting and highlighting `.delete-zone`,
so the reviewer sees the shortened row up close rather than having to find it.
The first declaration was wrong and the handoff verifier caught it: I had
deep-linked `/work?task=0001` with the `drawer:statusDetails` fixture, but that
fixture seeds task `9999` (the `SHOT_PREVIEW_FIXTURE_TASK_ID`) and pins the
drawer to the Debug tab's status view, so `.delete-zone` never mounted and the
verify step failed with "highlight matched nothing". I re-read the fixture code
in `shot-preview-fixtures.ts` and WorkView's `?tab=` deep-link handling, chose a
fixture that seeds a plain review task and leaves the tab alone, pointed the
route at `?task=9999&tab=details`, and confirmed the fix by capturing the
element myself with `repoos shot --selector .delete-zone` before re-requesting
handoff — the capture shows the three buttons reading Delete / Archive / Hold.

## Approaches tried

My first instinct was to run the affected tests with bare `bunx vitest`, which
failed with "Install @vitejs/plugin-vue to handle .vue files" — the repo's test
entry is the `bun run test` wrapper (a documented two-pass wrapper that supplies
the Vue plugin and repo config), not a direct vitest call. Rerunning through
the wrapper passed everything, including the always-run safety file the wrapper
adds. That matches the AGENTS.md convention ("never bare `bun test`") and
confirms why it exists.

For the search phase I grepped the whole tree for "Delete task", "Archive task",
"Hold task", "Unarchive" and "Release hold" once and classified every hit into
four buckets before editing: (1) live UI copy, (2) live assertions, (3) live
docs/comments, (4) immutable history. That prevented both under-editing and
over-editing — the tempting mistake would have been "fixing" wording inside
old task files, which are records of what the UI said at the time.

## Challenges and blockers

None substantive. Two things needed care rather than effort:

1. The `repoos update --shots` command runs from the worktree but writes the
   canonical board copy in the main checkout (the CLI warns about this), so the
   worktree copy of the task file does not show the Shots section. I verified
   via `repoos api GET /api/tasks/1232` that the section landed, rather than
   hand-editing the file, which AGENTS.md forbids.
2. A stale "agent exited with an error / needs input" note appeared in the task
   activity from a crash-recovery event earlier in the session (pid reaping at
   14:51, before my body updates). It is unrelated to this work and no action
   was needed; the API shows the task `active` with the shots recorded.

## Key learnings

- **Copy changes are assertion changes.** Every label shortened here was
  anchored somewhere else — a test's `.toEqual`, a `toContain`, a
  `includes("Hold task")` locator, a doc sentence. A full-tree grep before and
  after the edit is the cheap way to prove none were missed; I re-grepped after
  the edits and only dialog titles and the new aria-labels still contain the
  word "task", all intentional.
- **Prefer structural assertions over substring assertions when labels shrink.**
  "Delete task" → "Delete" makes `toContain("Archive")`-style checks
  collision-prone (e.g. against "Unarchive"-adjacent copy). Asserting the
  element via its stable `data-test-id` survives future copy edits.
- **Exact-match locators beat `includes()`** for buttons that have busy-state
  variants: `trim() === "Hold"` cannot accidentally match "Holding…" the way a
  broader substring could.
- The repo's vitest wrapper is load-bearing; running vitest directly skips the
  Vue plugin and produces a confusing parse error that looks like a broken
  component rather than a wrong invocation.
- **Shot plans must be read against the fixture's own code.** Drawer fixtures
  each seed a task and may force a tab; `drawer:statusDetails` exists for the
  Debug-tab status view (#0972) and seeds id `9999`. A declared shot's route,
  `state` and `highlight` only work if the fixture actually mounts that DOM on
  that route — and `repoos shot <route> --selector …` against the preview is the
  cheap way to prove it before the handoff verifier does.
